metadata.title: A Dog Class
metadata.description: Define a class with a constructor that stores state on self and a method that prints it.

instructions.main: Define `class Dog` with `__init__(self, name, age)` that stores `self.name` and `self.age`, and `bark(self)` printing `<name> says woof!`. Then construct `dog = Dog("Rex", 3)` and call `dog.bark()`.
steps: Add the constructor `def __init__(self, name, age):` and store `self.name = name` and `self.age = age`.
Add `def bark(self):` with `print(f"{self.name} says woof!")`, then run it with `dog = Dog("Rex", 3)` and `dog.bark()` — the output is `Rex says woof!`.

hints.message: Define `class Dog:` with `def __init__(self, name, age):` storing `self.name = name`, a `def bark(self):` printing the woof line, then `dog = Dog("Rex", 3)` and `dog.bark()`.
`Dog("Rex", 3)` needs a constructor — add `def __init__(self, name, age):` so the class can receive the name and age when it is created.
`__init__` receives `self` but never stores anything on it — add `self.name = name` and `self.age = age`, otherwise `dog.name` doesn't exist and `bark` crashes.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: Your Dog class constructs with name and age, stores them on self, and barks correctly.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Construct `dog = Dog("Rex", 3)` and call `dog.bark()` so it prints `Rex says woof!` on its own line.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: The class, the constructor, and the method are all defined.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Define all three pieces: `class Dog:`, a `def __init__(self, name, age):` constructor, and a `def bark(self):` method inside the class.
